attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps the core: big tech executives are trying to undermine the newly agreed compromise after the deal was reached.

contract.note: An ordinary plain reading: several executives at large tech companies opposing or trying to weaken the deal from Dec 9 to Dec 12, 2023. Keeping trade associations separate from company executives is reasonable.

evidence.note: A dated CCIA Europe statement from Dec 9, 2023, asking for changes after the deal. It is a trade-association statement and names no big-tech company executives, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: The only item shows a trade association pushing for changes after the agreement. Nothing in the packet identifies several big-tech executives or what they did between Dec 9 and 12, and nothing rebuts the claim. The evidence does not settle it either way.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Faithful. Marcus says the first mention of foundation models, which he equates with general-purpose AI, came in mid-May 2022. The 'before ChatGPT' detail comes from his own context.

contract.note: Marcus himself grouped general-purpose AI with foundation models, so treating an earlier mention of general-purpose AI as a counterexample follows his own wording.

evidence.note: Council document 14278/21, a Slovenian Presidency compromise text dated Nov 29, 2021. It has a title and an Article 52a dedicated to general-purpose AI systems, about six months before May 2022.

reviews.rationale: An authenticated Council negotiating text from November 2021 already mentions general-purpose AI explicitly, with its own Article 52a. That meets the contract's condition for contradiction: May 2022 was not the first mention.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words. He is characterising LeCun's phrase, but the judgement that it misrepresents the record is his.

semantics.note: The testable core is the timeline: rules for foundation models were not a last-minute addition. 'Massive, massive' is rhetorical intensity and cannot be measured.

contract.note: The result depends on reading 'late' as 'last minute', but Marcus supplied that reading himself, so the contract follows his own words. LeCun's full statement was not recovered, which the packet lists as a gap.

evidence.note: Council document 9029/22, a French Presidency text dated May 13, 2022, in a faithful hosted copy. It refers to requirements for general-purpose AI in Article 4b and exempts SMEs from them, which shows proposed duties long before December 2023.

reviews.rationale: A dated negotiating text from May 2022 already proposes substantive duties for general-purpose AI, so this kind of regulation was not first added in the December 2023 final talks. That meets the support condition. It does not date every final obligation, and the intensity of 'massive' cannot be scored.
